disposition_reason: The only printed heavy metal values are Pb, Cd and Hg in the dried crayfish shell used to make chitosan; chitin results are figure-only and the finished chitosan was not reported numerically.

study.design: Laboratory extraction study producing chitosan from invasive crayfish shells by different demineralization and deproteinization routes, testing coating properties
study.origin: Faxonius limosus from the Danube River, Serbia
study.method: Pb and Cd: flame AAS (Varian SpectrAA-10) after dry ashing (EN 14082); Hg and other metals: AAS
study.qa: No CRM, recovery or LOD reported

material.label_as_printed: Crayfish shell, boiled and dried, raw material for chitosan (Faxonius limosus)

findings.group: Danube River crayfish shells, Novi Sad
findings.notes: Shell raw material, not finished chitosan; chitin and chitosan metal values are shown only in Figure 4 (log scale). Pb and Cd by flame AAS after dry ashing; Hg by AAS. Duplicate tests, repeated three times.

controls.control: demineralization (HCl to pH 1.3 or 0.5) and one deproteinization step
controls.outcome: Metal contents strongly reduced in chitin DM1.3 and further in DM0.5 (Ca 2% and 0.02% of shell); Pb, Cd and Hg values for chitin are figure-only (Figure 4)

unresolved: Pb, Cd and Hg in chitin and finished chitosan are shown only in Figure 4 on a log scale; no values recorded.
Basis of shell results not labelled; shells were oven dried before analysis.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 maximum level for crustacean meat, cited
regulatory_or_exposure.value: 0.5 mg/kg for Pb, Cd and Hg
